record.prompt: Our new product photos are up to 64 megapixels. resize/pipeline.py downscales everything to 40 MP before sending it to Tamberline. Look at their changelog at https://tamberline.example/changelog and tell me whether we can drop that step.
record.final_answer:
Yes — you can drop it, with one caveat.

What the changelog says (v2.6, 2026-09-14): source images up to 100 megapixels are accepted; anything larger still gets HTTP 413. The code's guard (resize/pipeline.py:4) exists solely for that old limit — "Tamberline rejects larger sources" — and 64 MP is comfortably under 100 MP.

Two things worth knowing before you delete it:

1. Keep a guard, just raise it. Deleting the block entirely means the next 100+ MP source (panorama stitch, medium-format camera, someone's composited TIFF) gets a hard 413 with no local warning. Changing the constant to 100_000_000 keeps the failure local and readable. Account/endpoint must actually be on v2.6 — the changelog describes what the API now does, not what your key is provisioned for.

2. The downscale was also costing you output resolution. Output is still capped at 8,000 px on the long side (unchanged in v2.6). A 64 MP 4:3 shot is roughly 9238x6928; the 40 MP cap shrinks that to ~7303x5477 — under the output cap. So today you're feeding Tamberline less than it would serve back. Dropping the step gets you renditions up to the full 8000 px long side.

So it's not just neutral cleanup: less CPU locally, slightly sharper web renditions. The only real risk is memory — decoding 64 MP in lumenpix is ~256 MB at 4 bytes/px, plus the resize buffer today — so check that worker memory is fine once several photos process concurrently.

Want me to change the constant to 100 MP (one-line patch) rather than delete the block?
